reconstructed_theorem_text: For every natural number n, including zero, let rho := Measure.haarMeasure(top : PositiveCompacts(O(n))), the actual Haar measure on the full real orthogonal group O(n) normalized to give the entire group mass one. Then rho is a probability measure and a Haar measure. Moreover, every Borel measure mu on O(n) that is a probability measure and a Haar measure equals rho. Here O(n) = {A in R^(n x n) : A^T A = I} has the inherited finite real matrix topology and Borel sigma-algebra; Haar means left invariant, finite on compact sets, and positive on nonempty open sets. There is no determinant-one restriction.
objects: The full orthogonal group O(n), the explicitly constructed measure rho = Measure.haarMeasure(top : PositiveCompacts(O(n))), and arbitrary competing Borel measures mu on O(n).
domains: n is any natural number, including zero. O(n) consists of real Fin n by Fin n matrices satisfying A^T A = I, without a determinant-one restriction. Its topology is inherited from finite real matrices and its measurable structure is Borel. O(0) is a singleton.
quantifiers: For every n, define rho locally. Assert IsProbabilityMeasure rho and rho.IsHaarMeasure; then for every measure mu, if IsProbabilityMeasure mu and mu.IsHaarMeasure, conclude mu = rho.
assumptions: There are no additional caller assumptions on n or O(n); compactness, nonemptiness, Hausdorffness and second countability are internally available. In the uniqueness clause only, the competing mu must have total mass one and satisfy the Haar property.
conclusion: The explicit constructor rho is probability and Haar, and any probability Haar measure mu on this same group is equal to rho as a measure.
scopes: The local rho depends on the universally quantified n and is fixed throughout its property and uniqueness clauses. The two assumptions on mu apply only to the competing measure in that clause. This asserts uniqueness among probability Haar measures, not among all measures; it does not separately assert right invariance or an algorithm.
constant_dependencies: rho depends only on n and the fixed group topology and Borel structure; its constructor is normalized on top, the entire group, with mass one. There are no free numerical constants, and rho does not depend on the competing mu.
